title: Meet S, T and U
goal: Recognise, name and write S, T, U.
cue: A letter has a name. Later, we will learn the sounds it can represent in words. Today, say the letter names.
spelling: A letter has a name. Later, we will learn the sounds it can represent in words. Today, say the letter names.

dialogue.name: Heart
dialogue.text: Can you find the letter T?

dialogue.name: Puck
dialogue.text: Yes. It is between S and U.

task: Point to S and U. Say their names, then write their lowercase partners.
story: The letter S has a big form and a small form.
reviewPrompt: Recall two letters from day 6 before looking back.

cards.title: Letter S
sections: sun /sʌn/ · the star that lights our day
In sun, s represents /s/. This is a word sound, not the letter name.
Write S and s three times. Cover the model and write the pair again.

articulation.label: Letter S
articulation.alt: Letter S: /ɛ/ → /s/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /ɛ/: Front tongue; open the jaw a little more.
/s/: Make a narrow gap near the ridge; let air flow.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.

cards.title: Letter T
sections: tea /ti/ · a drink made with leaves and water
In tea, t represents /t/. This is a word sound, not the letter name.
Write T and t three times. Cover the model and write the pair again.

articulation.alt: Letter T: /t/ → /i/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.

articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.

cards.title: Letter U
sections: umbrella /ʌmˈbrɛlə/ · something that keeps rain off you
In umbrella, u represents /ʌ/. This is a word sound, not the letter name.
Write U and u three times. Cover the model and write the pair again.

articulation.label: Letter U
articulation.alt: Letter U: /j/ → /u/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /j/: Front tongue high; glide into the next vowel.
/u/: High back tongue; round the lips.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.

cards.title: Five words to hear and use
sections: the star that lights our day. The sun is hot.
the highest part of something. The top of the box is red.
a cover held over you to keep rain off. Puck has a raincoat but no umbrella.
soft clothing worn on the foot inside a shoe. He also buys white socks.
Toward a higher place. Put your hand up.
Listen to each word. Point or act to show its meaning. Say one word, then one short sentence. Ask for help with spelling patterns you have not learned yet.
